sect1.title: libglvnd-&libglvnd-version;
sect1.sect2:
Introduction to libglvnd
The libglvnd package dispatches OpenGL API calls to a given driver vendor at runtime. Some of the libraries are simply wrappers to the main dispatcher. Drivers that are built with libglvnd in mind provide their own OpenGL functionality. For , it will install libEGL_mesa and libGLX_mesa. For NVIDIA, it will provide libEGL_nvidia, libGLX_nvidia, and others. Each implementation is specific to the driver it comes from. The benefit of doing it this way is that a driver doesn't have to obey to the architecture an OpenGL vendor uses, nor does it have to be absorbed by the vendor.
If you've come here from the BLFS Mesa page, please read for information regarding how to navigate BLFS, compatibility, and transitioning.

libglvnd Dependencies
If is not installed, this package will not provide libGL or libGLX. libOpenGL will still be built. Many build systems will expect libGL to be present, so it is heavily recommended to install before installing this package.

sect2.title: Installation of libglvnd
sect2.para: Some non-Mesa drivers will expose one or two EGL device extensions from EGL_EXT_device_base, EGL_EXT_device_enumeration, and EGL_EXT_device_query. Some packages require that all three extensions are present, although historically base proves that enumeration and query is possible, since the latter two are newer extensions that separate the former into two. Apply a patch to make libglvnd advertise all three if one is present:
Install libglvnd by running the following commands:

screen.userinput:
mkdir build && cd build &&
meson setup --prefix=/usr \ --buildtype=release \ -D hgl=false \ .. &&
ninja

sect2.title: lib32 Installation of libglvnd
sect2.para: Install lib32-libglvnd by running the following commands:

screen.userinput: DESTDIR=$PWD/DESTDIR ninja install && cp -vr DESTDIR/usr/lib32/* /usr/lib32 && rm -rf DESTDIR && ldconfig
